items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: Donald Novis, who was a singer, also went to Pasadena School with me. He sang a chorus of it and I played behind him, and all that kind of stuff.

ctx.x: -- that unusual in the band at that time.

No, I came into the band as a soloist. When Irving Mills heard me in California -- the Cotton Club -- I was doing a solo in the show. And this particular night, as I think I told you, was when Donald Novis, one of the fine singers of that period -- he went got to Pasadena the same time I did. And so, I played this "Trees" in the show at the Cotton Club. And he asked Don to sing the chorus, or take a chorus of it. And he did. So, therefore we were playing together this same number.

But even though other musicians were soloists before they joined Duke, they did not always solo immediately with Duke, and so the fact that you did I thought might be unusual. I think it was in terms of the later day band. But --
